label: Consumer loan
narrative:
I am writing to formally dispute the reporting practices of Credit Acceptance Corporation concerning an auto loan I obtained from them. I believe that Credit Acceptance Corporation has violated my rights under 15 U.S.C. 6802 and 15 U.S.C. 6801 by failing to properly inform me of my right to opt out of having this loan information reported to my consumer report. 
 
 Under 15 U.S.C. 6801, financial institutions have a continuing obligation to respect a consumer 's privacy, and 15 U.S.C. 6802 grants consumers the right to opt out of having their information reported to credit bureaus. Credit Acceptance Corporation did not conspicuously inform me of this right to opt out before reporting the loan information to my consumer report. The lack of such notification constitutes a breach of their obligation under these statutes. 
 
 I request that the CFPB investigate this matter and compel Credit Acceptance Corporation to provide evidence of their compliance with these privacy requirements. Specifically, I am seeking confirmation that they notified me of my right to opt out and that they provided this information in a clear and conspicuous manner. 
 
 Additionally, I am serving this letter as both a formal complaint against Credit Acceptance Corporation and as a pre-arbitration notice. Should my consumer rights not be respected and this account is not removed from my credit report after being notified of these violations, I will proceed with arbitration to address these issues and seek appropriate remedies for the infringement of my rights. 
 
 Please review this matter and provide guidance on the steps taken to resolve this dispute. I would appreciate a written response detailing the actions the CFPB will take to address my concerns. 
 
 Thank you for your prompt attention to this issue. 
 
 Sincerely, XXXX XXXX
